sections.overview: The European mink is a semi-aquatic mustelid tied to riverbanks and wetlands. Once widespread across Europe, it now survives in a few isolated populations and is classified as Critically Endangered, one of the most threatened carnivores on the continent.
sections.identification: A medium-sized mustelid with a long body, short legs and a short tail, measuring roughly 32–50 cm from head to tail and weighing from about half a kilogram to a little over one kilogram, males being larger. The coat is glossy brown to almost black. White patches cover both the upper and lower lips, whereas the American mink has white only on the lower lip and chin.
sections.habitat: It needs riverbanks for both food and shelter, and lives along small and medium rivers, streams, swamps, riparian forest and wet meadows; large river deltas such as the Danube’s are important. It digs its own burrow, uses an abandoned water vole burrow or shelters among tree roots.
sections.diet: It is a generalist predator of amphibians, small mammals, fish, birds and aquatic invertebrates. Amphibians were long thought to dominate its diet, but data from the Danube Delta do not support this: what it eats varies with the season and the environment.
sections.behavior: The European mink is solitary, adults pairing only in the breeding season. It is most active around dusk and before dawn.
sections.reproduction: Mating takes place from late February to March, and females do not delay pregnancy. Gestation lasts 35–42 days and a litter holds three to seven kits, raised by the female alone. Young are weaned at about ten weeks and become sexually mature at roughly one year.
sections.ecology: As a predator of aquatic and semi-aquatic animals, it sits in riverside food webs. Its main current rival is the introduced American mink, which competes with it directly for the same riverbank habitat.
sections.conservation: It is listed as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List and occupies less than a fifth of its former range, in isolated populations in northern Spain and south-western France, the Danube Delta and parts of Russia. A small population has been re-established on Hiiumaa Island in Estonia. Where American mink are absent, habitat destruction and persecution for its fur remain the main threats. It is protected under the EU Habitats Directive and is extinct in the Czech Republic.
